title: The Business Model (How we make money)

parts.visual:
A startup has millions of free users, but they are going bankrupt because they don't know how to charge them. They have a product, but they do not have a Business Model.

The Models:
1. SaaS (Software as a Service): Monthly subscriptions.
2. Marketplace: Taking a % cut of a transaction between two people (Uber, Airbnb).
3. Freemium: 95% use it for free, 5% pay for premium features.
4. Enterprise B2B: Selling massive, multi-year contracts directly to other corporations.
parts.audio: A great product is not a company. A Business Model explains exactly how the startup extracts money from the value it creates. The most popular models in tech are SaaS, Marketplaces, and Enterprise B2B.

questions.question: Airbnb doesn't own any hotels. They simply connect people who have extra rooms with people who need to sleep, and charge a 15% fee on every booking. What is this Business Model?
options: A Marketplace Model (or Brokerage Model). They facilitate the transaction and take a 'Take Rate' (commission).
questions.correct_answer: A Marketplace Model (or Brokerage Model). They facilitate the transaction and take a 'Take Rate' (commission).
questions.explanation: Marketplaces are incredibly hard to start (the Cold Start Problem), but wildly profitable once they achieve network effects.

questions.question: Listen to the B2B founder. How do they price their software?
questions.tts_text: We don't charge a flat monthly fee. We charge $0.01 for every single API call the customer makes. If they use our system a little, they pay a little. If they scale, they pay millions.
options: Usage-Based Pricing (or Pay-As-You-Go). The revenue scales perfectly with the customer's utilization of the product.
questions.correct_answer: Usage-Based Pricing (or Pay-As-You-Go). The revenue scales perfectly with the customer's utilization of the product.
questions.explanation: This is how AWS (Amazon Web Services) and Stripe make billions of dollars.

questions.question: What is the danger of relying on an 'Advertising' business model (like early Facebook or Twitter)?
options: You need hundreds of millions of daily active users before the ad revenue becomes mathematically significant. Most startups die long before they reach that scale.
The ads take up too much memory.
questions.correct_answer: You need hundreds of millions of daily active users before the ad revenue becomes mathematically significant. Most startups die long before they reach that scale.
questions.explanation: If you don't charge the user, you must achieve planetary scale.

questions.question: Why do VCs love 'Enterprise B2B' business models?
options: Because the contracts are massive ($100k+ per year) and 'Churn' is extremely low. Once a massive corporation installs your software, it is too painful for them to switch to a competitor.
questions.correct_answer: Because the contracts are massive ($100k+ per year) and 'Churn' is extremely low. Once a massive corporation installs your software, it is too painful for them to switch to a competitor.
questions.explanation: High ACV (Annual Contract Value) + Low Churn = A billion dollar valuation.
